managed_cloud.note: AGI Managed Cloud's own retention: conversations are kept until the user deletes them or the account, with no automatic expiry enforced today; temporary chats expire in about 30 days by a daily job (https://agiworkforce.com/privacy). There is no mode where AGI itself stores nothing: the workspace zero-data-retention setting controls which upstream model providers a request may route to, not AGI's own storage of the conversation. Training commitment is at https://agiworkforce.com/terms section 05: AGI does not train AGI-owned models on submitted content, explicitly not a promise about a third-party model provider's handling. Data is hosted in the United States only; AGI does not offer EU or UK data residency (https://agiworkforce.com/privacy#s-08).

openai.note: Abuse-monitoring logs are held up to 30 days unless the law requires longer. Zero data retention needs prior approval and drops the request from those logs. Regional processing covers the United States, the European Economic Area with Switzerland, and the United Arab Emirates; the other listed regions are storage only.
openai.cacheTokenBillingNote: usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens is documented as "Cached tokens present in the prompt," and the prompt-caching cost formula (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching) computes weighted cost as ordinary_input_tokens + cached_tokens * cacheInputMultiplier, deriving ordinary_input_tokens from prompt_tokens minus the cached and cache-write counts. Cached tokens are a subset of prompt_tokens, not additional to it.

anthropic.note: API inputs and outputs are deleted within 30 days of receipt, with exceptions for the Files API, custom agreements, usage-policy enforcement and legal holds. Zero data retention exists as a separate agreement. No residency region list is published.
anthropic.cacheTokenBillingNote: The usage object reports cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens separately from input_tokens: total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens, so cached tokens are additional to, not a subset of, input_tokens. This provider speaks the Anthropic Messages wire protocol directly and shares its usage-object shape (harnesses.json).

google.note: On the paid tier Google does not use prompts, cached content, files or responses to improve its products. Prompts and responses are still logged for a limited period to detect abuse. The terms name no zero-retention option and no region list.
google.cacheTokenBillingNote: UsageMetadata.promptTokenCount is documented as: "When cachedContent is set, this is still the total effective prompt size meaning this includes the number of tokens in the cached content." cachedContentTokenCount is a subset of promptTokenCount, not additional to it.
google.reasoningTokenBillingNote: UsageMetadata documents totalTokenCount as "Total token count for the generation request (prompt + thoughts + response candidates)", and candidatesTokenCount as the tokens across the generated candidates only, so thoughtsTokenCount is additional to the reported output count rather than a subset of it. The published Gemini API pricing table charges thinking tokens at the output rate (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing).

open_router.note: Zero retention is a per-request data policy that restricts the upstream pool, not a default, and the docs state the setting has no bearing on OpenRouter's own handling. The condition on this class is that the adapter honours the requirement per request: a request carrying the zero-retention requirement is sent with the deny data-collection policy, and the harness declares that through the zeroDataRetentionOnRequest feature, which is what admission reads. A request without the requirement sends nothing, so the pool narrows only for the organizations that asked.

vercel_gateway.note: Gateway's own layer is zero retention: Vercel states AI Gateway does not retain prompts, outputs or sensitive data and deletes user data immediately after a request completes, and does not use prompts or responses for training (https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training). Upstream retention follows the provider that serves, so the class is conditional: the per-request providerOptions.gateway.zeroDataRetention flag, free on Pro and Enterprise, restricts routing to providers Vercel holds zero-retention agreements with (Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Google Vertex, Groq, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Together, Cerebras, Mistral, Moonshot and others on the published list) and fails the request with no_providers_available when none serves the model. The condition on this class is that the adapter sends that flag for a zero-retention workspace, which the vercel_gateway harness declares as zeroDataRetentionOnRequest. Anthropic excludes its newest frontier model from zero retention on every provider (30-day retention, not used for training); the routes data is what says which model that is today. Provider prompt caching is at the provider's layer and its retention follows the provider. No residency commitment is published. Retrieved 2026-09-06.

cheaperinference.note: Gateway's own layer only, operated by Keak: Cheaper Inference does not store prompt or response bodies in its application database, request content is transmitted to the serving provider, and temporary uploads expire after one hour (https://platform.cheaperinference.com/legal/dpa). Retention therefore follows the upstream host that serves each request, which the gateway picks per request from its supply; its public catalog marks a zero_data_retention flag and a zero_data_retention_route per model, but the API exposes no request-level control that restricts routing to those hosts, so the class is conditional and no route on this gateway is admitted for a zero-retention workspace until such a control exists and the adapter sends it. Operational logs are retained up to 12 months, account and billing records for the agreement term plus seven years. Keak states it does not use customer prompt or response bodies to train Keak models. Data may be processed in the United States, Canada, Europe, and other countries where Keak operates. Re-read 2026-09-06.

bedrock.note: Gateway's own layer (AWS), not the upstream model provider. Retention is set by a data_retention_mode the customer configures at account or project scope: none is zero data retention, no request or response data is written to durable storage by AWS or shared with the model provider; default applies the model's own retention behavior; aws_review and legacy provider_data_share retain content up to 30 days within the AWS boundary for AWS-performed human review some model providers require as a condition of access, content is never shared with the provider. Some models require aws_review as their minimum and do not permit none without a support-assisted eligibility process, contact your AWS account manager to discuss eligibility. AWS FAQ states AWS and third-party model providers will not use any inputs to or outputs from Amazon Bedrock to train Amazon Nova, Amazon Titan, or any third-party models (https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/faqs/). Bedrock is offered across many AWS regions the customer selects for inference; no fixed region list is recorded here. Upstream model provider policy still applies per model and is not covered by this record.

groq.note: Groq's general privacy policy explicitly excludes GroqCloud, which is instead governed by the Groq Services Agreement and this Customer Data Processing Addendum. The DPA states data is retained for the time period needed to accomplish the purposes of processing unless applicable law requires longer, and that the customer may request deletion of personal data within a maximum period of 180 days. No dedicated zero-data-retention API feature is published, only this request-based deletion within up to 180 days, so this is recorded as unavailable rather than on_request. The DPA restricts processing to providing, maintaining and supporting the Cloud Services and to the customer's documented instructions, but does not explicitly state whether Groq trains models on customer data, so trainsOnInputs is left unknown. Personal data may be transferred to and processed in the United States and other countries where Groq or its subprocessors maintain processing operations, no fixed region list.

experientiallabs.note: Gateway's own layer only, operated by Resolute Labs AI, Inc. (Delaware) as Experiential Labs. Retention follows the rung that serves a request: the keyless catalog (GET /api/models) carries a per-model retention verdict computed over the lanes the gateway actually routes (zdr_all_rungs, zdr_enforceable, not_zdr) and each provider row a zero_data_retention flag, and the organisation policy require-ZDR (settings/data-controls) restricts routing to zero-retention lanes; the condition on this class is that the founder turns that control on for the company organisation. Responses API continuations are retained 24 hours unless store:false; nothing is stored with the upstream provider either way. Training on inputs is unverified: the public website privacy policy (https://www.experientiallabs.ai/privacy, 2026-09-04) covers only the marketing site and states the platform is a separate service outside it, and the platform's own policy requires sign-in. The website policy names United States processing for its own data; no residency commitment is published for the gateway, so no region is claimed. Upstream model providers retain inputs under their own practices per rung; that policy applies per model and is not covered here.
